CheckKind.description: Category of a readiness check, so clients can group them in a UI.
CheckKind.title: CheckKind

DependencyCheck.description: Result of probing exactly one dependency.

detail.description: Probe-specific facts. Must never contain secrets or credentials.
detail.title: Detail

error.description: Human-readable failure reason when status is not ok.
error.title: Error

required.description: Whether failure makes the service NOT_READY. Computed from settings (KEN_REQUIRE_PGVECTOR, KEN_REQUIRE_OLLAMA) so one binary can be lenient in native development and strict elsewhere.
required.title: Required

DependencyCheck.title: DependencyCheck

ErrorCode.description:
Stable machine-readable error codes.

Codes are ``snake_case``. A client may branch on a code but must never
branch on ``message``, which is human-readable and may be reworded at any
time. Adding a member in a later phase is additive and non-breaking.
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

ErrorDetail.description: One field-level or item-level problem within a failed request.

location.description: Dotted path to the offending field, when applicable.
location.title: Location

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail

ErrorResponse.description:
The ONLY error body any endpoint returns.

Deliberately does not carry a stack trace, an exception class name or a
database message: backend-engineer.md forbids exposing internal
exceptions. ``request_id`` is how a caller correlates a failure with the
server logs instead.

message.description: Human-readable summary. Never branch on this.
message.title: Message

request_id.description: Correlates this failure with server logs.
request_id.title: Request Id

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

HealthResponse.description: ``GET /health`` -- liveness only. No dependency is consulted.
HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

HealthStatus.description:
Status of a single dependency check.

Distinct from :class:`~ken_contracts.health.ReadinessStatus`: a dependency
is *described* by this enum, whereas the service as a whole is *judged* by
an aggregate verdict.
HealthStatus.title: HealthStatus

MetaResponse.description:
``GET /meta`` -- build and configuration facts.

``settings`` is an explicit allowlist built in the router. Secrets are
never placed in this payload; see docs/CONTRACTS.md.

auto_approve_enabled.description: Must be false in v1 (TRD.md section 20). Enforced by a Settings validator.
auto_approve_enabled.title: Auto Approve Enabled

MetaResponse.title: MetaResponse

ReadinessResponse.description:
``GET /ready`` -- aggregate readiness.

HTTP status mapping, implemented in the router and asserted by tests:

==================  =====  ===============================
aggregate status    code   headers
==================  =====  ===============================
ready               200    Cache-Control: no-store
degraded            200    Cache-Control: no-store
not_ready           503    no-store, Retry-After: 5
==================  =====  ===============================

A probe that itself raises yields 503 with that check marked ERROR -- never
a 500, because an unhandled exception in a readiness probe is still a
readiness answer.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

ReadinessStatus.description:
Aggregate verdict over all dependency checks.

The distinction between DEGRADED and NOT_READY is the whole point of the
``required`` flag on each check: an optional dependency that is missing
degrades the service without making it unready. In Phase 0 pgvector and
Ollama are both optional, so their absence must not take the API down.
ReadinessStatus.title: ReadinessStatus

ServiceIdentity.description: Who is answering. Present in every health, readiness and meta payload.

git_sha.description: Short commit SHA when discoverable, else null.
git_sha.title: Git Sha

version.description: Application version from the distribution metadata.
version.title: Version

ServiceIdentity.title: ServiceIdentity

503.description: A required dependency is not ready.
